s: At which Congress Session was the Working Committee authorised to launch a programme of Civil Disobedience?
x: The Lahore Session of the Indian National Congress (December 1929) formally adopted Purna Swaraj (complete independence) as its objective. On 31 December 1929, the tricolour was hoisted, symbolizing the break from colonial rule. The session also explicitly resolved to launch a programme of civil disobedience under Gandhi's leadership, which directly led to the Dandi March in March 1930 and the nationwide Salt Satyagraha.

s: Which of the following was not included in the resolutions of Lahore Session of Congress in 1929?

x: The resolutions proposed by Indian National Congress on December 31, 1929 AD consisted of following points- (1) There is no benefit from Round Table Conference. (4) All India Congress whenever it considers appropriate can start Civil-Disobedience Movement. Abolition of Untouchability was not mentioned in the proposal. The Round Table Conference can be considered as India’s foreign policy as the British Government only had the right to make a foreign policy of India. It was primarily passed in Congress session of 1921 A.D. that there must be a foreign policy for India.

s: "Sedition has become my religion" was the famous statement given by Gandhiji at the time of
o: publicly violating Salt Law at Dandi
attending the Second Round Table Conference in London

x: The statement was made during the launch of the Civil Disobedience Movement in 1930. Gandhiji began the movement with the historic Dandi March on 12th March 1930. Accompanied by 78 selected followers, he walked nearly 200 miles from Sabarmati Ashram to Dandi on the Gujarat coast. On reaching Dandi, he symbolically broke the Salt Law by making salt, openly defying British authority. At that moment, Gandhiji declared: "The British rule in India has brought about moral, material, cultural, and spiritual ruination of this great country." I regard this rule as a curse. I am out to destroy this system or the government. Sedition has become my religion. Ours is a nonviolent battle. We are not to kill anybody, but it is our dharma to see that the curse of this Government is blotted out".

Salt was a major point of the movement because the English Government had banned the selling of the salt and also imposed a tax on it, which highly affected the poor. Mahatma Gandhi started Dandi March accompanied by 80 of his trusted volunteers from Sabarmati Ashram on March 12, 1930 A.D. s: Which one of the following began with the Dandi March?

On April 5, 1930 A.D. he reached Dandi and on 6 April he violated the salt law, manufacturing salt by boiling seawater. This marked the beginning of the Civil Disobedience Movement. Gandhi-Irwin Pact *Viceroy Irwin released Gandhiji from jail on 26th January 1931 AD considering the increasing influence of the Civil Disobedience Movement. Talks between Gandhiji and Irwin started in February 1931 AD with the efforts of Tej Bahadur Sapru and M.R. Jaykar. Gandhi-Irwin Pact was signed on 5th March, 1931. Sarojini Naidu termed Irwin and Gandhiji as ‘Two Mahatmas’. According to this pact - (1) Under the leadership of Gandhiji, Congress decided to withdraw the Civil Disobedience Movement, (2) All political prisoners who had not convicted of violence were to be released, (3) Right to peaceful protest at shops of foreign cloth and liquor shops, (4) Permission to make salt in the Coastal States without Salt Tax, (5) Congress agreed to participate in the Second Round Table Conference. People were disappointed by this pact because it did not include the commulation of the death sentences of Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev and Rajguru. Biographer of Irwin, Alan Campbell Johnson termed the benefits to Gandhi in Gandhi-Irwin Pact as consolation prizes and said this pact was the only surrender of Irwin agreeing to enter into negotiations. 1. s: Tripuraneni Ramaswamy Chowdary's song "Veeragandhamu Techhinaramu... Veerulevvaro Telpudee" belongs to which movement?

s: Pedaganjam and Chinaganjam were known for their production of
x:
Pedaganjam and Chinaganjam, located in the present-day Prakasam district, were historically famous for salt production. Their coastal location and extensive salt pans made them important centres for manufacturing and trading salt during both the pre-colonial and British periods. Salt production formed an important part of the local economy, and the region contributed significantly to the salt trade along the Coromandel Coast. During the British period, salt became an important source of government revenue through the imposition of the Salt Tax, which later became the focus of Gandhiji's Civil Disobedience Movement. Although the region also engaged in agriculture and trade, Pedaganjam and Chinaganjam are particularly remembered for their salt industry. Hence, the correct answer is Option (4).
Exam Note:
• Pedaganjam – Salt production
• Chinaganjam – Salt production
• Present District – Prakasam

s: Who of the following organized a march on the Tanjore coast to break the Salt Law in April in 1930?
x: The Vedaranyam March or Vedaranyam Satyagraha was organized to protest the salt tax imposed by the British Empire in India. The march took place in April 1930 A.D. and was the second of its kind, following the Dandi March organized by Mahatma Gandhi, both in the framework of the Civil Disobedience Movement. The Vedaranyam March was a group of volunteers under the leadership of C. Rajagopalachari. It began at Trichinopoly (now Tiruchirappalli) and ended in Vedaranyam, a small coastal town in Tanjore (in present day Vedaranyam beach of Nagapatinam district). By collecting salt directly from the sea, the marchers broke the Salt Law.
